channel.title: Web3 Hub
channel.description: Web3 Hub reports crypto news: Bitcoin and Ethereum, exchanges, DeFi protocols, stablecoins, regulation, security incidents and network upgrades.

item.title: Token freezes can stop a TRON swap at the contract
item.description: A TRON token freeze can make a balance visible but unusable in a swap; the block usually comes from token contract rules, not TRON’s native staking freeze.

item.title: Check the Token and Router Before a TRON Swap
item.description: Find a TRON swap contract by matching the token address, checking the router and quote, then comparing liquidity, fees and execution risk before signing.

item.title: A fast bridge quote does not prove finality
item.description: A bridge's fast quote can reflect fronted liquidity, not settled source-chain finality; check confirmations, proof design and exit rules before moving assets.

item.title: How Bungee Handles Cross-Chain Token Swaps
item.description: Bungee combines token swaps and bridge routes in one quote; fees, delivery time and destination gas still depend on the route and chains you choose.

item.title: Wrapped and native tokens on Manta Pacific serve different roles
item.description: On Manta Pacific, a wrapped balance can represent an asset bridged from elsewhere, while a native token originates on the network; the contract address tells you which you hold.

item.title: Bridge Fees Can Buy Faster Withdrawals, at a Price
item.description: Paying a bridge fee can shorten a withdrawal by buying liquidity, but compare the total cost, route, settlement risk and destination chain before signing.

item.title: How to tell if tracked wallets are buying a falling token
item.description: A falling token’s chart cannot confirm accumulation: verify tracked-wallet swaps, net balances, pool liquidity and timing before treating a purchase as a signal.

item.title: Check the USDT Network Before You Send
item.description: Match the network on the receiving USDT deposit page to the sender’s withdrawal route, then check the address, fee and any memo before you send.

item.title: Thin TRON Liquidity Raises Treasury Swap Costs
item.description: A TRON treasury swap gets a worse rate when its order is large against pool reserves; checking route depth, fees and execution limits helps control cost.

item.title: TRON swap guide: prepare a wallet for team payouts
item.description: A team payout on TRON starts with the right token, a funded sending wallet and checked recipient addresses; here is how to plan each step.

item.title: Why XMR Bridges Wait for Confirmations
item.description: An XMR bridge waits for blocks on Monero before releasing tokens elsewhere, using confirmations to reduce reorg risk; each bridge sets its own release threshold.

item.title: Monero Restore Height Can Hide a Bridge Refund
item.description: Monero restore height sets the first block a wallet scans; if it starts too late, a bridge refund may stay hidden until the wallet rescans from earlier.

item.title: Why Bridges Pause During Chain Hard Forks
item.description: Bridges pause around hard forks because validators and relayers need one canonical chain, reliable finality and compatible software before transfers resume.

item.title: Cross-chain swap quote changed? Check the route and minimum
item.description: A cross-chain quote changes when prices, network costs or routes move; check the minimum receive amount, selected route and quote expiry before approving.

item.title: Treasury teams need two-sided records to reconcile Polygon Bridge flows
item.description: Treasury teams should match Polygon PoS transfers across source and destination records, separate pending withdrawals from settled funds and value each leg consistently.

item.title: Polygon Bridge: Check Token Support and Contracts in 2026
item.description: Check the Ethereum root token and Polygon child contract before using Polygon Bridge; a matching name or visible balance alone does not confirm a valid route.

item.title: Five Rules for Omnichain Treasury Governance
item.description: Five controls for shared state, spending authority, settlement checks and recovery can keep a multichain treasury accountable when transfers cross networks.

item.title: How Omnichain Tokens Keep One Supply Across Blockchains
item.description: Omnichain tokens move balances across chains by burning, locking, minting or releasing units; the accounting model determines what counts toward supply.

item.title: Five checks to make cross-chain transfers faster and cheaper
item.description: Compare the amount delivered, every network and bridge fee, route steps, slippage and destination details before signing; the cheapest quote can change.

item.title: Frequent Cross-Chain Swaps: Compare Pools and Relayers
item.description: Frequent cross-chain traders should compare the full route: pool depth, relayer execution, fees, slippage and destination delivery can change the best choice.
